page_title: How we ship code faster and safer with feature flags

sources.entry: How we ship code faster and safer with feature flags, Github.

summary.title: How we ship code faster and safer with feature flags
summary.one_liner: GitHub's account of how feature flags reduce deployment risk, enable incremental development in small batches, and how they handle flag strategies, actor types, and flag cleanup.
keywords: ci builds with flags enabled and disabled
takeaways: Wrapping risky changes behind a feature flag lets you disable them in seconds instead of rolling back a deployment.
Feature flags let teams merge small batches of work without long-lived feature branches, which eases review and reduces merge conflicts.
Shipping strategies include individual actors, staff-only shipping, early access groups, percentage of actors, and dark shipping for percentage of calls.
Choose what to flag based on the change: users for visual changes, repositories for data storage changes, GitHub Apps for API changes.
Flags carry runtime and technical debt costs, so GitHub automated removal of dead code from fully rolled-out flags with a script.
summary.summary: This GitHub engineering blog post explains how the company uses feature flags to lower deployment risk and to build new features incrementally. It covers testing with flags in development, CI builds with all flags on or off, and production overrides via query string. It describes shipping strategies (individual actors, staff shipping, beta groups, percentage of actors, dark shipping) and how to pick the actor type to flag. It closes with the runtime and technical debt costs of flags and a script that automates removing stale flag code.
